title: Compute Shader
summary: Official Derivative overview of compute shaders, covering general GPU thread dispatch, arbitrary texture reads and writes, the difference from vertex/pixel rasterization, GLSL version requirements, and GLSL TOP compute mode.
guidance: Use this article when a plan needs GPU work that is not naturally tied to one rasterized output pixel or one material fragment.
A pixel shader writes the hard-wired output pixel once per render pass, while a compute shader can read textures and write values at arbitrary locations.
Require GLSL 4.30 or later for compute-shader plans.
For TOP workflows, use GLSL TOP compute mode when the output should be written by dispatch threads instead of regular image rasterization.
